newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt will export at least 600,000 T rice in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Egypt will export at least 600,000 T rice in 96/97.

text.p: Egypt will export at least 600,000 tonnes of rice in the 1996/97 marketing year from an expected harvest of 2.8 million tonnes, the state's Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills said on Wednesday.
Company chairman Kamal Ghoneim told Reuters the firm would accept purchase orders from October 15 and a committee would set the export price two weeks later.

Last year Egypt exported 340,000 to 350,000 tonnes of rice, from a harvest of 2.6 million tonnes, to Libya, Jordan, Syria and Iraq. Israel, the former Soviet republics and Turkey also buy Egyptian rice.
A company official said Egyptian rice was competitive in quality, but its relatively high price and small quantities rule out any contest with the giant Asian and Indian producers.
"Our rice is high quality and has a special taste which a lot of countries want but it costs too much to produce so we sell it at higher prices," the official said.

But Hamdi Farag, the head of the holding company's commercial section, said, "This year an export policy will be adopted to ensure that Egyptian rice competes with other varieties on foreign markets."
